entries.title: Psalms 142:1
segments: Title, when he was in the cave; probably the cave of Adullam, to which he fled from Achish king of Gath in a friendless condition.  It was there that he began to collect a band.

entries.title: Psalms 142:2
segments: The more our troubles are multiplied, the more earnest and importunate should we be in our prayers.  God loves to have us bring before his throne all our sorrows, perplexities, and dangers.

entries.title: Psalms 142:3
segments: Knewest my path; knewest it as a friend, able and willing to direct, defend, and help.

entries.title: Psalms 142:4
segments: I looked on my right hand--cared for my soul; or, Look thou on [my] right hand, and see; for there is no man who will know me: refuge has failed me; no man careth for my soul.  He mentions his right hand, because it is there that a helper should naturally stand.

entries.title: Psalms 142:5
segments: When all earthly succor fails, we are called to stay our souls upon God, who always cares for us and will help us.

entries.title: Psalms 142:6
segments: God's help makes the weakest of his servants stronger than the mightiest among their foes.

entries.title: Psalms 142:7
segments:
Out of prison; David was so hemmed in by his enemies that he was like a man in prison. 
 
  The righteous shall compass me about; as my sympathizing friends. 
 
When God delivers a righteous man from trouble, all the good rejoice with him.
